en: How far is the penalty spot from the goal?
es: ¿A qué distancia de la portería está el punto penal?
cs: ¿A qué distancia está el penalty spot from the goal?
answer: The penalty mark is 11 m (12 yds) out, measured from the midpoint between the two goalposts.
note: L1.6 describes the penalty area and gives the distance of the penalty mark from the goal.

en: How much does a match ball have to weigh?
es: ¿Cuánto tiene que pesar el balón en un partido?
cs: How much tiene que pesar el balón at the start of the game?
answer: Between 410 g and 450 g (14 to 16 oz) at the start of the match.
note: L2.1 lists the required qualities of the ball, including its weight range.

en: How long is the half-time break allowed to be?
es: ¿Cuánto puede durar el descanso del medio tiempo?
cs: ¿Cuánto puede durar el halftime break, like what's the max?
answer: No more than 15 minutes; the competition rules set the exact length and only the referee can allow a change.
note: L7.2 sets the upper limit for the half-time interval and says who fixes its duration.

en: What color does a player's head cover have to be?
es: ¿De qué color tiene que ser el protector de cabeza de un jugador?
cs: If a player wears a head cover, ¿de qué color tiene que ser?
answer: Black or the same main color as the shirt, and teammates who wear one must all use the same color. Goalkeepers' caps are not covered by this rule.
note: L4.4.1 is the head covers subsection and its first requirement is the color.

en: What are the six confederations in world football?
es: ¿Cuáles son las seis confederaciones del fútbol mundial?
cs: ¿Cuáles son las six confederations del fútbol mundial?
answer: AFC (Asia), CAF (Africa), Concacaf (North and Central America and the Caribbean), CONMEBOL (South America), OFC (Oceania) and UEFA (Europe).
note: The glossary entry for Confederation names all six and their regions.

en: What counts as an outside agent in soccer?
es: ¿Qué se considera un agente externo en el fútbol?
cs: What counts como agente externo in a soccer game?
answer: Any animal, object or structure, plus any person who is neither a match official nor on a team list as a player, substitute or team official.
note: The glossary entry defines the term in full. A shorter definition also sits in L3.7, which is a held-out law and cannot be gold here.

en: A defender trips a forward who is standing exactly on the white paint that outlines the keeper's box. Does that count as in the box or not?
es: Un defensa le mete zancadilla a un delantero que está parado justo sobre la raya blanca donde empieza el territorio del portero. ¿Eso ya cuenta como adentro o no?
cs: Un defensa trips a forward que está parado exactly on the white paint del box del portero. ¿Eso cuenta como adentro or not?
answer: Yes. The lines are part of the areas they enclose, which puts a player standing on the line inside the area.
note: L1.2 states that the lines belong to the areas they bound. Avoided EN: line, area, boundary, mark, belong, field, ball, player, edge, outside, penalty. Avoided ES: línea, área, zona, terreno, demarcar, delimitar, balón, jugador, borde.

en: Why does the game keep going after the clock hits 45 or 90, and who gets to say how much longer it runs?
es: ¿Por qué el partido sigue después de que el reloj marca 45 o 90, y quién dice cuánto más se alarga?
cs: ¿Por qué sigue el partido after the clock hits 45 or 90, y quién dice how much longer it goes?
answer: The referee makes up for playing time lost in that half to things like substitutions, injuries, time-wasting, cards, VAR delays and goal celebrations. The referee sets the amount, the fourth official shows the minimum, and it can go up but not down.
note: L7.3 lists the causes of lost time and says who decides and displays the amount; also: G.football-terms.additional-time for the first half of the question only. Avoided EN: allowance, time, lost, half, additional, added, minute, referee, fourth official, substitution, decide. Avoided ES: tiempo, perdido, periodo, prolongar, recuperar, añadir, árbitro, minuto, juego, decisión.

en: Can I keep my wedding ring on during a game if I wrap it up with athletic wrap?
es: ¿Puedo dejarme puesto el anillo de matrimonio cuando estoy en la cancha si lo envuelvo bien con una venda?
cs: ¿Puedo dejarme el wedding ring puesto during a game si lo envuelvo con athletic wrap?
answer: Only if it is not dangerous and is safely and securely covered. Anything the referee judges dangerous has to come off; wrapping or covering it is not enough.
note: L4.1 covers accessories and says dangerous items must be removed, not covered. Avoided EN: dangerous, equipment, accessory, wear, covered, taped, tape, remove, item, safe, player, match. Avoided ES: peligroso, equipamiento, accesorio, llevar, cubrir, cinta, quitarse, objeto, prenda, jugador, juego, partido.

en: Can a sponsor's brand be painted on the grass while the game is going on?
es: ¿Se puede pintar la marca de un patrocinador en el pasto mientras rueda el balón?
cs: ¿Se puede pintar el brand de un sponsor on the grass mientras rueda el balón?
answer: No. No commercial advertising is allowed on the field of play, or on the ground within 1 m of its boundary lines, from when the teams come out until half-time and again from their return until the end of the match.
note: L1.12 bans commercial advertising on the field of play during those periods; L1.13 is about official logos and emblems, not sponsors. Avoided EN: commercial, advertising, field, play, ground, match, area, lines, permitted, real, virtual. Avoided ES: publicidad, comercial, terreno, juego, jugar, superficie, suelo, partido, área, líneas.

en: Which kinds of calls can the crew sitting at the monitors away from the pitch step in on?
es: ¿En qué tipo de situaciones se pueden meter los que están frente a las pantallas en la cabina?
cs: ¿En qué tipo de calls se pueden meter los que están at the monitors, the crew en la cabina?
answer: Only a clear and obvious error or a serious missed incident involving a goal or no goal, a penalty or no penalty, a red card (including a clearly wrong second yellow), or the referee booking or sending off the wrong player.
note: L6.5 lists the four situations in which the VAR may assist; also: G.referee-terms.video-match-officials-vmos, which mentions reviewable categories without listing them. Avoided EN: video, assistant, referee, VAR, official, replay, footage, review, check, decision, error, incident, goal, penalty, card, watch, television. Avoided ES: vídeo, árbitro, asistente, VAR, arbitral, imágenes, revisión, chequeo, decisión, error, incidente, gol, penal, tarjeta, jugada, ver, televisión.

en: A two-legged series finishes level on aggregate. What breaks the deadlock in favor of the side that found the net more as visitors?
es: Una serie a dos juegos queda igualada en el global. ¿Qué criterio favorece al que más la metió de visitante?
cs: Una serie a dos juegos queda level on aggregate. ¿Qué criterio favorece al team que más la metió as visitors?
answer: The away goals rule: when both teams have the same number of goals over the tie, goals scored away from home count double.
note: The glossary entry defines the away goals rule; also: L10.2, which only names it as a permitted procedure. Avoided EN: away, goals, home, scored, tie, match, teams, count, double, method, deciding, same, number. Avoided ES: goles, tantos, marcados, anotado, fuera, casa, eliminatoria, partido, encuentro, vuelta, doble, equipos, cuentan.

en: During a penalty kick the ball bursts on its way toward goal, before it touches the keeper or the frame of the goal. What is the ruling?
es: En un penal, el balón se poncha en el camino hacia la portería, antes de tocar al portero o a los postes. ¿Qué marca el árbitro?
cs: En un penal the ball pops on its way to goal, antes de tocar al portero or the post. ¿Qué marca el ref?
answer: The penalty kick is retaken, because the ball became defective while moving forward and before touching a player, the crossbar or the goalposts.
note: L2.2 has a specific sentence for a ball that becomes defective during a penalty kick before it touches anyone or the goal frame.

en: A striker's boot comes off by accident in a goalmouth scramble and, before he can put it back on, he scores with that foot. Does the goal count?
es: A un delantero se le sale el zapato sin querer en un barullo en el área y, antes de poder ponérselo otra vez, mete gol con ese pie. ¿Vale el gol?
cs: Al delantero se le sale el cleat by accident en un scramble en el área y, antes de ponérselo, he scores con ese pie. ¿Vale el gol?
answer: Yes, the goal is awarded. A player who loses footwear accidentally has until the ball next goes out of play to replace it, and a goal scored before then stands.
note: The last paragraph of L4.2 covers footwear or a shinguard lost by accident and says a goal scored before replacing it counts.

en: A player who was sent to the sideline to fix his kit runs back on without the referee's OK. The referee stops play just to book him, and the player had not touched the ball or gotten in anyone's way. How does play restart?
es: Un jugador que salió a la banda para arreglar su uniforme se vuelve a meter sin permiso del árbitro. El árbitro para el juego solo para amonestarlo, y el jugador no había tocado el balón ni estorbado a nadie. ¿Cómo se reanuda el juego?
cs: Un jugador que salió a la banda to fix his kit se mete otra vez without the ref's OK. El árbitro para el juego just to book him, y el jugador no había tocado el balón ni estorbado a nadie. How does play restart?
answer: The player is cautioned and play restarts with an indirect free kick from where the ball was when play was stopped, since there was no interference.
note: The last paragraph of L4.6 gives the caution and the restart for re-entering without permission, with and without interference.

en: Furious about a disallowed goal, a substitute storms into the room where the video officials are working. What does the referee do?
es: Furioso porque anularon un gol, un suplente se mete a la sala donde están trabajando los del VAR. ¿Qué hace el árbitro?
cs: Furioso por un disallowed goal, un suplente se mete al room where the VAR guys are working. ¿Qué hace el árbitro?
answer: The substitute is sent off. Any player, substitute, substituted player or team official who enters the video operation room gets a red card.
note: L1.14.1 describes the video operation room and states the sanction for entering it; also: L12.4.8, which lists it among sending-off offences.

en: The referee awards a penalty just as the 45 minutes of the first half run out. Does he blow for half-time, or is the kick taken first?
es: El árbitro marca penal justo cuando se cumplen los 45 minutos del primer tiempo. ¿Pita el descanso o primero se cobra el penal?
cs: El árbitro marca penal right as the 45 minutes run out en el primer tiempo. ¿Pita el descanso or is the kick taken first?
answer: The kick is taken first. The half is extended until the penalty kick has been completed.
note: L7.4 says a half is extended for a penalty kick that has to be taken or retaken; also: L14.1, which says the same and defines when the kick is completed.

en: The crossbar snaps during a match and there is no way to repair it. What happens to the match, and does it get played again later?
es: Se rompe el travesaño a medio partido y no hay manera de repararlo. ¿Qué pasa con el partido, y se vuelve a jugar después?
cs: Se rompe el travesaño in the middle of the match y no hay manera de repararlo. What happens to the game, y se vuelve a jugar después?
answer: The match must be abandoned, and an abandoned match is replayed unless the competition rules or organisers decide otherwise.
note: L1.10.0 says a crossbar that cannot be repaired means the match is abandoned; L7.5 says what happens to an abandoned match. The Spanish edition uses 'suspender (definitivamente)' for abandon.

en: Not counting stoppage time, what is the most playing time a match can have if it goes to extra time?
es: Sin contar el tiempo añadido, ¿cuánto es lo máximo que se puede jugar en un partido que se va a tiempos extra?
cs: Sin contar el stoppage time, what's the most playing time que puede tener un partido if it goes to extra time?
answer: 120 minutes: two halves of 45 minutes, plus two extra-time periods of at most 15 minutes each.
note: L7.1 gives the two 45-minute halves and the glossary entry for extra time gives the two periods of up to 15 minutes; also: L10.2 in place of the glossary entry. The 120 total is a sum the reader has to make from the two passages.

en: A substitute is about to come on wearing something dangerous. Which official is supposed to catch that, and what happens if he refuses to take it off?
es: Un suplente está por entrar y trae puesto algo peligroso. ¿A cuál de los árbitros le toca detectarlo, y qué pasa si el jugador no se lo quiere quitar?
cs: Un suplente está por entrar wearing something dangerous. Which official is supposed to catch that, y qué pasa si no se lo quiere quitar?
answer: Checking a substitute's equipment is one of the fourth official's tasks. A substitute must be inspected before entering and told to remove the item, and a player who refuses to comply must be cautioned.
note: L6.2 assigns the equipment check of substitutes to the fourth official; L4.1 gives the inspection before entering, the order to remove the item and the caution for refusing.

en: What does the team that wins the coin toss get to choose before kick-off?
es: ¿Qué puede elegir el equipo que gana el volado antes del saque inicial?
cs: El equipo que gana el coin toss, ¿qué le toca escoger, el lado de la cancha o el kick-off?
answer: The toss winner picks either which goal to attack in the first half or to take the kick-off, and the other team gets whichever option is left.
note: L8.1.1 opens with the coin toss and the two choices available to the winner.

en: Can you be offside from a throw-in?
es: ¿Hay fuera de juego en un saque de banda?
cs: ¿Te pueden marcar offside directo de un throw-in?
answer: No. There is no offside offence when a player receives the ball directly from a throw-in, and the same goes for a goal kick and a corner kick.
note: L11.3 lists the three restarts from which receiving the ball directly is never an offside offence.

en: Can a player who got a red card during the match take a kick in the penalty shoot-out?
es: ¿Un jugador que fue expulsado durante el partido puede tirar en la tanda de penales?
cs: Si a un jugador le sacaron la roja during the game, ¿todavía puede tirar en los penalties?
answer: No. A player sent off during the match may not take part in the shoot-out.
note: L10.3.0 states that a player sent off during the match is not permitted to take part in the shoot-out.

en: How far away do opponents have to stand from the player taking a throw-in?
es: ¿A qué distancia tienen que estar los rivales del que hace el saque de banda?
cs: En un throw-in, ¿qué tan lejos tiene que pararse el defender del que saca?
answer: At least 2 m (2 yds) from the point on the touchline where the throw-in is to be taken.
note: L15.1 sets the 2 m minimum distance in the throw-in procedure; also: L15.2, which repeats the distance when describing the sanction.

en: On a corner kick, does the ball have to leave the corner area before it is in play?
es: En un tiro de esquina, ¿el balón tiene que salir del cuadrante para estar en juego?
cs: En un corner kick, ¿la pelota tiene que salir del corner area para que ya esté in play?
answer: No. The ball is in play as soon as it is kicked and clearly moves; it does not need to leave the corner area.
note: L17.1 says when the ball is in play at a corner kick and that leaving the corner area is not required.

en: How far back does the wall have to be at a free kick?
es: ¿A qué distancia tiene que ponerse la barrera en un tiro libre?
cs: En un free kick, ¿a cuántas yardas tiene que estar la barrera from the ball?
answer: Opponents must stay at least 9.15 m (10 yds) from the ball until it is in play, unless they are standing on their own goal line between the goalposts.
note: L13.2 gives the required distance for opponents at every free kick and its goal line exception; also: L13.3, which cites the same distance when describing the sanction.

en: Does the goalkeeper have to stay on the goal line during a penalty kick?
es: ¿El portero tiene que quedarse sobre la línea de gol en un penal?
cs: En un penal, ¿el goalie tiene que quedarse on the line hasta que le peguen al balón?
answer: Yes. The goalkeeper stays on the goal line between the posts, facing the kicker, until the ball is kicked, and at the moment of the kick must have at least part of one foot touching, in line with, or behind the goal line.
note: L14.1 contains both the requirement to remain on the goal line until the kick and the one foot rule at the moment of the kick; the consequences of breaking it are in L14.2.

en: When the assistant with the flag decides whether a striker had run too far ahead of the defenders, does an elbow or a sleeve sticking out in front matter?
es: Cuando el abanderado decide si un delantero se había ido demasiado adelante de los defensas, ¿importa que solo le sobresalga el codo o la manga?
cs: Cuando el linesman decide si el delantero was too far ahead de los defensas, ¿cuenta si nomás el codo is sticking out?
answer: No. Hands and arms are ignored for every player; only the head, body and feet count, and the arm is taken to start at the bottom of the armpit.
note: L11.1 defines which body parts are used to judge the position and excludes hands and arms; avoided: offside, position, player, head, body, feet, hands, arms, armpit, opponent, second-last, goal line, halfway line, ball, level (es: fuera de juego, posición, jugador, cabeza, tronco, pierna, manos, brazos, axila, adversario, penúltimo, línea, balón).

en: If a shot smacks the woodwork and bounces back onto the pitch, do they carry on or is there a stoppage?
es: Si un disparo pega en el palo y regresa a la cancha, ¿se sigue o se para el partido?
cs: Si el tiro pega en el palo and bounces back a la cancha, ¿siguen o lo paran?
answer: They carry on. The ball stays in play when it comes back off a goalpost, the crossbar or a corner flagpost and remains on the field.
note: L9.2 says the ball is still in play after coming off the goal frame or corner flagpost if it stays on the field; avoided: ball, in play, rebound, goalpost, crossbar, corner flagpost, remains, field of play, match official (es: balón, juego, rebote, poste, travesaño, banderín, permanezca, terreno).

en: Does it count if the man in gloves hurls it by hand from his own box all the way into the net at the far end with nobody else touching it?
es: ¿Cuenta el tanto si el arquero avienta la pelota con el brazo desde su área y se mete en el arco de enfrente sin que nadie más la toque?
cs: ¿Cuenta si el arquero la avienta from his own box y se mete all the way en el arco de enfrente?
answer: No. If the goalkeeper throws the ball directly into the opponents' goal, no goal is given and the other team gets a goal kick.
note: L10.1 has the specific sentence on a goalkeeper's throw going straight into the other goal; avoided: goal, scored, goalkeeper, throws, directly, opponents, goal kick, ball, awarded (es: gol, guardameta, lanza, mano, portería, directamente, contraria, saque de meta, balón).

en: When the whistle goes because somebody is hurt and there was no foul, which side is handed it back afterwards?
es: Cuando pitan para atender a un lesionado y no hubo falta, ¿a quién le devuelven la pelota al seguir?
cs: Cuando pitan porque alguien is hurt y no hubo foul, ¿a quién le dan la pelota when they start again?
answer: It is a dropped ball: for the defending goalkeeper if the ball was inside the penalty area, otherwise for a player of the team that would have kept or won possession, or, if the referee cannot tell, the team that last touched it.
note: L8.2.1 sets out who receives a dropped ball depending on where the ball was when play stopped; also: L8.0 for why the restart is a dropped ball; avoided: dropped ball, referee, play, stopped, ball, team, player, possession, retained, gained, touched, penalty area, goalkeeper, restart (es: balón a tierra, árbitro, juego, detener, balón, equipo, jugador, posesión, conservado, ganado, tocó, área penal, guardameta, reanudación).

en: What gesture tells everyone that a set piece needs a second person involved before it can count, and when is the official allowed to drop that gesture?
es: ¿Con qué ademán avisa el silbante que en un cobro a pelota parada hace falta que alguien más intervenga para que valga la anotación, y hasta cuándo lo tiene que sostener?
cs: ¿Qué seña hace el silbante to let everyone know que en ese set piece alguien más tiene que intervenir before it counts, y cuándo la puede bajar?
answer: The referee raises an arm above the head and keeps it up until the kick has been taken and the ball touches another player, goes out of play, or it is clear a goal cannot be scored directly.
note: L13.1.1 describes the indirect free kick signal and how long it is held; avoided: referee, indicates, indirect, free kick, raising, arm, head, signal, maintained, taken, ball, touches, player, goal, scored, directly (es: árbitro, indicar, tiro libre, indirecto, levantar, brazo, cabeza, señal, mantener, balón, toque, jugador, gol, marcar, directamente).

en: From twelve yards, may the shooter pause at the end of his approach and pretend to strike, sending the man between the sticks the wrong way, before actually hitting it?
es: Desde los once pasos, ¿puede el cobrador frenarse al terminar su impulso y amagar el disparo para engañar al arquero antes de pegarle a la pelota?
cs: Desde los once pasos, ¿el cobrador puede frenarse at the end of his approach y amagar para engañar al arquero, or is that not allowed?
answer: No. A dummy during the run-up is allowed, but feinting to kick once the run-up is finished is an offence: the referee restarts with an indirect free kick for the defending team whether or not the ball went in, and cautions the kicker.
note: L14.2 lists feinting after completing the run-up among the kicker offences that always lead to an indirect free kick and a caution; avoided: penalty, kick, kicker, feinting, run-up, completed, goalkeeper, ball, goal, cautions, indirect free kick, referee (es: penal, tiro, ejecutor, lanzador, finta, carrera, finalizado, guardameta, balón, golpear, portería, amonestar, libre indirecto, árbitro).

en: When someone on the sideline stalls instead of putting it back in, just to burn the clock, what does the official do, and can their rivals wind up with it?
es: Cuando alguien hace tiempo en el lateral y no acaba de meterla a la cancha, ¿qué hace el juez y se la pueden dar al rival?
cs: Cuando alguien está wasting time en el lateral y no la mete, ¿qué hace el juez, and can their rivals wind up with it?
answer: The referee whistles and starts a visible five-second countdown with a raised hand; if the throw-in has not been taken when it runs out, the throw-in goes to the opposing team. The player is only cautioned for excessive further delay after that.
note: L15.2 describes the five-second countdown for a delayed throw-in and the switch of the throw to the opponents; avoided: throw-in, delaying, unfairly, taking, player, team, referee, whistle, signal, five seconds, countdown, raised hand, awarded, opposing, cautioned, ball (es: saque de banda, retrasar, ejecución, jugador, equipo, árbitro, silbato, señalar, cuenta atrás, cinco segundos, mano levantada, conceder, adversario, amonestar, balón).

en: A midfielder's pass strikes the referee in the centre circle and rolls to an opponent, who sets off on a counter-attack. Does play go on, and if not, how does it restart?
es: El pase de un mediocampista le pega al árbitro en el círculo central y el balón le queda a un rival, que arranca un contragolpe. ¿Sigue la jugada? Si no, ¿cómo se reanuda?
cs: El pase le pega al ref en media cancha y la pelota le queda al otro equipo, que se va en counter-attack. ¿Sigue el juego or does the ref stop it, y cómo se reanuda?
answer: Play does not go on. The ball is out of play because it touched a match official, stayed on the field and the team in possession changed, and play restarts with a dropped ball.
note: L9.1 lists a ball that touches a match official followed by a change of possession as out of play and names the dropped ball restart; also: L8.2.1 for who receives the dropped ball.

en: A through ball is played toward a striker standing behind the back line. A centre back with time and a clear view swings a foot to clear it, mishits it, and it runs straight to that striker, who scores. Does the goal stand?
es: Mandan un pase filtrado hacia un delantero que está detrás de la línea defensiva. Un central, con tiempo y viendo bien el balón, intenta despejar con el pie, le pega mal y se lo deja al delantero, que anota. ¿Vale el gol?
cs: Mandan un through ball a un delantero que está behind the back line. El central, con tiempo y viéndola clarito, tries to clear it, le pega mal y se la deja al delantero, que mete gol. ¿Vale o es offside?
answer: Yes. The defender deliberately played the ball, and a failed clearance still counts as deliberate play, which means the striker is not treated as having gained an advantage from the offside position.
note: L11.2 covers receiving the ball from an opponent's deliberate play, says an unsuccessful clearance is still deliberate, and gives the time and clear view indicators.

en: After a sliding tackle, a defender ends up off the pitch behind his own goal line and stays there without the referee's permission. Seconds later a pass reaches an attacker who has only the goalkeeper between him and that goal line. Is the attacker offside?
es: Tras una barrida, un defensa queda fuera de la cancha, detrás de su propia línea de meta, y se queda ahí sin permiso del árbitro. Segundos después le llega un pase a un atacante que solo tiene al portero entre él y esa línea. ¿Está en fuera de juego?
cs: Después de una barrida, el defensa se queda off the field, detrás de su goal line, sin permiso del ref. Luego le llega el pase a un atacante que nomás tiene al portero enfrente. ¿Es offside o no?
answer: No. A defender who leaves the field without permission is treated as standing on the goal line for offside until the next stoppage or until his team plays the ball out of its penalty area towards halfway, which leaves two opponents (the goalkeeper and that defender) not behind the attacker.
note: L11.4 has the rule that a defender off the field without permission counts as being on the goal line for offside; the general definition of the position is in L11.1.

en: The referee restarts with a dropped ball for a midfielder near the halfway line. As soon as it hits the ground he shoots from distance, and the ball flies into the opponents' goal without anyone else touching it. What is the decision?
es: El árbitro reanuda con un balón a tierra para un mediocampista cerca de la media cancha. En cuanto bota, el jugador dispara de lejos y el balón entra en la portería rival sin que nadie más lo toque. ¿Qué se marca?
cs: El ref hace un dropped ball para un mediocampista cerca de media cancha. He shoots right away y la pelota entra al arco rival sin que nadie más la toque. ¿Cuenta el gol o qué marcan?
answer: No goal. A dropped ball must touch at least two players before it can go in, and because it entered the opponents' goal the restart is a goal kick.
note: L8.2.2 gives the two-player requirement after a dropped ball and the goal kick restart when it enters the opponents' goal.

en: A cup final goes to a penalty shoot-out. One team finished extra time with ten players because of a red card, and the other still has eleven. What has to happen before the kicks begin?
es: Una final se va a la tanda de penales. Un equipo terminó los tiempos extra con diez jugadores por una expulsión y el otro sigue con once. ¿Qué tiene que pasar antes de que empiecen a tirar?
cs: La final se va a penalties. Un equipo acabó el extra time con diez por una roja y el otro tiene once. ¿Qué tienen que hacer before the shoot-out starts?
answer: The team with eleven must drop to ten by excluding one player and must tell the referee that player's name and number. The excluded player takes no part in the kicks, other than possibly replacing a goalkeeper who cannot continue.
note: L10.3.1 requires the team with more players to reduce to the same number as its opponents and to inform the referee of each excluded player.

en: A team is fouled in midfield and takes the free kick at once. A defender standing only about four yards away sticks out a leg and intercepts the pass. Does the referee order a retake?
es: A un equipo le cometen falta en media cancha y cobra el tiro libre de inmediato. Un defensa que estaba a unos cuatro metros estira la pierna e intercepta el pase. ¿El árbitro manda repetir el tiro?
cs: Les hacen falta en media cancha y cobran el free kick rapidito. Un defensa que estaba like four yards away mete la pierna y corta el pase. ¿El ref lo manda repetir or play on?
answer: No, play continues. When a free kick is taken quickly and an opponent closer than 9.15 m (10 yds) intercepts it, the referee lets play go on.
note: L13.3 has the quick free kick exception to the retake for an opponent inside the required distance.

en: A winger taking a corner taps the ball a yard out of the corner area and then dribbles it himself toward the box before any other player has touched it. What does the referee give?
es: Un extremo cobra un tiro de esquina, toca el balón un metro fuera del cuadrante y luego él mismo se lo lleva hacia el área antes de que lo toque otro jugador. ¿Qué marca el árbitro?
cs: El extremo cobra el corner, la toca tantito y luego he dribbles it himself hacia el área antes de que alguien más la toque. ¿Qué marca el ref?
answer: An indirect free kick to the defending team, because the kicker touched the ball a second time before it had touched another player.
note: L17.2 gives the indirect free kick for a corner taker who touches the ball again before another player does.

en: Can a goal be scored straight from a throw-in, and what about straight from a corner kick?
es: ¿Se puede meter gol directo de un saque de banda? ¿Y directo de un tiro de esquina?
cs: ¿Se puede meter gol directo from a throw-in? ¿Y de un corner kick, el gol olímpico sí vale?
answer: Not from a throw-in: if the ball goes straight into the opponents' goal it is a goal kick. From a corner kick yes, but only against the opposing team.
note: L15.0 says a goal cannot be scored directly from a throw-in and L17.0 says one can be scored directly from a corner kick; each half of the question needs its own passage.

en: If a player somehow sends the ball straight into his own team's goal from a kick-off, or straight from a free kick, is it an own goal in either case?
es: Si un jugador manda el balón directo a su propia portería en un saque inicial, o directo de un tiro libre, ¿cuenta como autogol en alguno de los dos casos?
cs: Si alguien manda la pelota straight into his own goal en el saque inicial, o directo de un free kick, ¿es autogol in either case?
answer: No in both cases. Whether it comes from a kick-off or from a direct or indirect free kick, a ball kicked directly into the kicker's own goal gives a corner kick to the opponents.
note: L8.1.1 covers the kick-off going directly into the kicker's own goal and L13.1.2 covers the same for free kicks; the two restarts are in different laws.

en: A defender's clearance hits the referee inside the defender's own penalty area and drops to an attacker a few yards away, still in the area. What does the referee do, and who gets the ball at the restart?
es: El despeje de un defensa le pega al árbitro dentro del área del propio defensa y el balón le cae a un atacante ahí mismo, todavía en el área. ¿Qué hace el árbitro y a quién le toca el balón en la reanudación?
cs: El despeje del defensa le pega al ref inside his own box y la pelota le cae a un atacante, todavía en el área. ¿Qué hace el ref, y quién se queda con la pelota on the restart?
answer: The referee stops play, because the ball touched a match official and possession changed, and restarts with a dropped ball. Since the ball was inside the penalty area, it is dropped for the defending team's goalkeeper.
note: L9.1 makes the ball out of play with a dropped ball restart after it hits the referee and possession changes, and L8.2.1 says a dropped ball inside the penalty area goes to the defending goalkeeper.

en: During a penalty shoot-out, where does each of the two goalkeepers have to be while a kick is taken: the one facing the kick and the one whose team-mate is taking it?
es: En una tanda de penales, ¿dónde tiene que colocarse cada uno de los dos porteros mientras se tira: el que ataja y el del equipo que está tirando?
cs: En los penalties, ¿dónde se tiene que parar cada portero while the kick is taken: el que ataja y el del equipo que está tirando?
answer: The goalkeeper facing the kick stays on the goal line between the posts, facing the kicker, until the ball is kicked. The kicker's own goalkeeper waits on the field outside the penalty area, on the goal line where it meets the penalty area boundary line.
note: L14.1 gives the defending goalkeeper's position at a penalty kick, which applies in the shoot-out, and L10.3.1 gives the position of the kicker's goalkeeper.

en: A goalkeeper catches a cross and holds on to the ball for well over eight seconds. What does the referee award, and from which side of the field is it taken?
es: Un portero atrapa un centro y se queda con el balón en las manos bastante más de ocho segundos. ¿Qué marca el árbitro y desde qué lado de la cancha se cobra?
cs: El portero atrapa un centro y se queda con la pelota way more than eight seconds. ¿Qué marca el ref, y de qué lado se cobra?
answer: A corner kick to the opponents, taken from the corner area nearest to where the goalkeeper was when penalised.
note: L12.3 awards a corner kick when a goalkeeper controls the ball with the hands for more than eight seconds and L17.1 says which corner area is used; also: L17.0 for the award itself.

en: Is taking your shirt off to celebrate a goal a yellow card, even if the goal ends up being disallowed?
es: ¿Quitarse la camiseta para festejar un gol es tarjeta amarilla, aunque después anulen el gol?
cs: Si te quitas la camiseta celebrating a goal, is that a yellow aunque después lo anulen?
answer: Yes. A player who removes the shirt while celebrating a goal must be cautioned, and that applies even when the goal is disallowed.
note: L12.4.6 lists removing the shirt among the celebration acts that must be cautioned even if the goal is disallowed.

en: For handball, where does the arm start? Does the shoulder count?
es: Para la mano, ¿desde dónde cuenta el brazo? ¿El hombro es mano?
cs: Para una handball, where does the arm start? ¿El hombro cuenta or not?
answer: The upper boundary of the arm is level with the bottom of the armpit, which leaves the shoulder above that line outside the handball zone.
note: L12.1.1 sets the upper boundary of the arm for handball at the bottom of the armpit.

en: Is a bicycle kick allowed, or is it dangerous play?
es: ¿Está permitida la chilena o se marca como juego peligroso?
cs: ¿La chilena is allowed, o te la marcan como dangerous play?
answer: A scissors or bicycle kick is allowed as long as it is not dangerous to an opponent.
note: L12.2.1 defines playing in a dangerous manner and says outright that a bicycle kick is permissible when it does not endanger an opponent.

en: Can the referee still show a card after the final whistle or during a penalty shoot-out?
es: ¿El árbitro todavía puede sacar tarjeta después del silbatazo final o durante la tanda de penales?
cs: ¿El árbitro todavía puede sacar tarjeta after the final whistle, o durante the penalty shootout?
answer: Yes. The referee's disciplinary authority runs from entering the field for the pre-match inspection until leaving it after the match ends, and that includes a penalty shoot-out.
note: L12.4.0 states the time span of the referee's authority to take disciplinary action, shoot-out included.

en: What counts as serious foul play?
es: ¿Qué se considera juego brusco grave?
cs: ¿Qué cuenta como serious foul play, like qué tan fuerte tiene que ser la entrada?
answer: A tackle or challenge for the ball that endangers an opponent's safety or uses excessive force or brutality, including a lunge from the front, side or behind with one or both legs.
note: L12.4.10 is the definition of serious foul play; also: L12.4.8 only lists it as a sending-off offence without defining it.

en: Can a coach get a yellow card for sarcastically clapping at the referee?
es: ¿Le pueden sacar amarilla a un entrenador por aplaudirle con sarcasmo al árbitro?
cs: Can a coach get a yellow por aplaudirle al árbitro in a sarcastic way?
answer: Yes. Sarcastic clapping is the example given of an action showing a clear lack of respect for the match officials, which is dissent and a caution offence for a team official.
note: L12.4.14 is the team-official caution list and names sarcastic clapping as an example of dissent by action.

en: When somebody on the bench misbehaves and the ref cannot tell who did it, who takes the punishment?
es: Si alguien de la banca hace algo indebido y el árbitro no logra saber quién fue, ¿quién carga con el castigo?
cs: If alguien en la banca hace algo indebido and the ref can't tell quién fue, who takes the punishment?
answer: The senior team coach present in the technical area receives the sanction.
note: L12.4.12 covers an unidentified offender from the technical area. Avoided: offence, committed, technical area, substitute, team official, offender, identified, senior, coach, sanction (es: infracción, área técnica, suplente, cuerpo técnico, infractor, identificar, sancionar, entrenador).

en: Someone takes a wild swing at a rival nowhere near the action and misses completely. What do the rules call that, and does missing get him off the hook?
es: Un futbolista le tira un puñetazo a un rival lejos de la pelota y ni lo roza. ¿Cómo le llama el reglamento a eso, y se salva por haber fallado?
cs: Alguien le tira un puñetazo a un rival away from the action and totally misses. ¿Cómo le llaman a eso in the rules, y se salva porque falló?
answer: It is violent conduct: using or trying to use excessive force against an opponent when not challenging for the ball counts whether or not contact is made.
note: L12.4.11 defines violent conduct and says it applies regardless of contact. Avoided: violent, conduct, player, excessive, force, brutality, opponent, challenging, ball, contact, strikes, deliberately, head, face, hand, arm (es: conducta violenta, jugador, fuerza, excesiva, brutalidad, adversario, disputar, balón, contacto, golpear, cabeza, cara, mano, brazo).

en: If someone shoves a rival while the game is stopped, say right after the whistle has gone, can that shove earn the other side a set piece?
es: Si alguien empuja a un rival con el partido parado, digamos justo después del silbatazo, ¿ese empujón le puede dar una falta a favor al otro equipo?
cs: Si alguien empuja a un rival when the game is already stopped, like right after the whistle, ¿ese empujón le da a set piece al otro equipo?
answer: No. Free kicks and penalty kicks can only be awarded for offences committed while the ball is in play.
note: L12.0 limits free kicks and penalties to offences with the ball in play; also: L12.5 (first sentence) and L8.0. Avoided: direct, indirect, free kick, penalty, awarded, offences, committed, ball, in play (es: tiro libre, directo, indirecto, penal, conceder, infracciones, cometidas, balón, en juego).

en: Is it legal to step in front of a rival who is chasing a pass that is still far from both of you, just to cut off his run, without touching him?
es: ¿Se vale atravesársele a un rival que va corriendo por un pase que todavía está lejos de los dos, nada más para cortarle la carrera y sin tocarlo?
cs: ¿Se vale meterte in front of a rival que va corriendo por un pase that's still far from both of you, just to cut off his run, sin tocarlo?
answer: No. Moving into an opponent's path to obstruct or slow them when the ball is not within playing distance of either player is impeding, although simply being in the way is not an offence.
note: L12.2.2 defines impeding without contact; also: L12.2.0 gives the indirect free kick for it. Avoided: impede, progress, opponent, moving, path, obstruct, block, slow, direction, ball, playing distance, player, position, way, shield, contact (es: obstaculizar, avance, adversario, interponerse, camino, obstruir, bloquear, ralentizar, dirección, balón, distancia de juego, jugador, posición, contacto).

en: What card does someone get for chucking a boot or a bottle at another person, and does it depend on how hard they hurl it?
es: ¿Qué tarjeta le toca a alguien que le avienta un zapato o una botella a otra persona, y cambia según qué tan duro se la aviente?
cs: ¿Qué tarjeta te toca if you chuck a boot o una botella at somebody, y cambia depending on qué tan duro la avientas?
answer: It depends on how it is done: done recklessly it is a caution for unsporting behaviour, and done with excessive force it is a sending-off for violent conduct.
note: L12.4.16 sets the sanction for thrown objects by degree. Avoided: thrown, object, ball, referee, disciplinary action, reckless, caution, offender, unsporting behaviour, excessive force, send off, violent conduct (es: lanzamiento, objetos, balón, árbitro, medida disciplinaria, temeraria, amonestar, infractor, conducta antideportiva, fuerza excesiva, expulsar, violenta).

en: After the whistle goes against his side, a defender boots it into the stands just to burn clock. What should happen to him?
es: Le pitan una falta en contra y un defensa revienta la pelota hasta la tribuna nada más para quemar tiempo. ¿Qué le debería pasar?
cs: Le pitan una falta en contra and the defender just boots it into the stands para quemar tiempo. What should happen to him?
answer: He must be cautioned for delaying the restart of play, since kicking the ball away after the referee has stopped play is one of the listed examples.
note: L12.4.7 lists kicking the ball away as delaying the restart; also: L12.4.4 names delaying the restart as cautionable. Avoided: referee, caution, player, delay, restart, play, kicking, carrying, ball, away, stopped, free kick, retake (es: árbitro, amonestar, jugador, retrasar, reanudación, juego, lanzar, balón, lejos, detenido, tiro libre, repetición).

en: A striker is through on goal inside the box when the last defender, with no chance of reaching the ball, grabs his shirt and drags him down. The referee gives the penalty. What card does the defender get?
es: Un delantero se va solo frente al portero dentro del área y el último defensa, sin ninguna posibilidad de llegar al balón, lo jala de la camiseta y lo tira. El árbitro marca penal. ¿Qué tarjeta le toca al defensa?
cs: El delantero is through on goal dentro del área y el último defensa, with no chance at the ball, lo jala de la camiseta and brings him down. The ref gives the penalty. ¿Qué tarjeta le toca al defensa?
answer: A red card. When a penalty is given for denying an obvious goal-scoring opportunity, the offender is only cautioned if the offence was an attempt to play or challenge for the ball; holding or pulling is a sending-off.
note: L12.4.9 separates the caution case (attempt to play the ball) from the sending-off case (holding, pulling, no possibility to play the ball) when a penalty is awarded.

en: A defender carelessly trips a striker who is clean through on goal just outside the box, the referee plays advantage, and the ball runs to a team-mate who scores. Does the defender still get a card?
es: Un defensa le mete una zancadilla a un delantero que se iba solo al arco, justo afuera del área; el árbitro da ley de la ventaja y el balón le queda a un compañero que mete el gol. ¿Todavía le sacan tarjeta al defensa?
cs: Un defensa trips the striker que se iba solo al arco, right outside the box, el árbitro da ventaja and a teammate scores. ¿Todavía le sacan tarjeta al defensa or no?
answer: No. Playing advantage on an offence that denied an obvious goal-scoring opportunity normally reduces the sanction to a caution, but when the non-offending team scores from that advantage there is no disciplinary sanction at all.
note: L12.4.3 covers advantage after a goal-scoring-opportunity offence and the exception when a goal results from the advantage.

en: A midfielder pulls back an opponent to stop a promising counter-attack and the referee decides to book him. Before the referee has started to show the card, the fouled team takes the free kick quickly with a clear chance to score. At the next stoppage, is the midfielder still booked?
es: Un mediocampista jala a un rival para cortar un contragolpe prometedor y el árbitro decide amonestarlo. Antes de que el árbitro empiece a sacar la tarjeta, el equipo que recibió la falta cobra rápido el tiro libre con una clara ocasión de gol. En la siguiente pausa, ¿todavía amonestan al mediocampista?
cs: Un mediocampista jala a un rival to kill a promising counter y el árbitro lo va a amonestar. But before he even pulls out the card, el otro equipo cobra rápido el free kick con una clara chance de gol. At the next stoppage, ¿todavía le sacan la amarilla?
answer: No. When the quick free kick is allowed in that situation, an offence that only stopped a promising attack is not cautioned at the next stoppage; an offence that denied an obvious goal-scoring opportunity would be a caution.
note: L12.4.2 is the quick free kick exception to delaying the restart to show a card and states what happens to the sanction afterwards.

en: A player who had stepped off for treatment runs back on without waiting for the referee's signal and immediately makes a reckless tackle on an opponent. Is that one yellow card or two?
es: Un jugador que había salido para que lo atendieran vuelve a entrar a la cancha sin esperar la señal del árbitro y de inmediato hace una entrada temeraria contra un rival. ¿Es una amarilla o son dos?
cs: Un jugador que salió for treatment se mete a la cancha again sin esperar al árbitro and right away goes in with a reckless tackle. ¿Es una amarilla or two?
answer: Two. Entering without permission and the reckless tackle are separate cautionable offences, and each one gets its own caution even when they happen close together.
note: L12.4.4 lists re-entering without permission as cautionable and gives this exact pairing as its example of two cautions; also: L12.4.8 for the second caution leading to a sending-off.

en: An attacker jumps for a cross, cannot reach it with his head and punches the ball into the net with his fist. The referee disallows the goal. What disciplinary sanction does the attacker get?
es: Un delantero salta por un centro, no alcanza con la cabeza y mete el balón a la red con el puño. El árbitro anula el gol. ¿Qué sanción disciplinaria le toca al delantero?
cs: El delantero salta for a cross, no alcanza con la cabeza and punches it into the net con el puño. The ref disallows the goal. ¿Qué sanción le toca?
answer: A caution for unsporting behaviour, because handling the ball in an attempt to score is cautionable whether or not the attempt succeeds.
note: L12.4.5 lists handling the ball in an attempt to score a goal among the cautions for unsporting behaviour.

en: The last defender, standing a step outside his own penalty area, has his arm stuck out wide and a shot heading for the empty net hits it by accident. The referee gives the handball. What colour card should he show?
es: El último defensa, parado un paso afuera de su área, tiene el brazo muy abierto y un tiro que iba a puerta vacía le pega ahí sin querer. El árbitro marca la mano. ¿De qué color debe ser la tarjeta?
cs: El último defensa está one step outside his own box con el brazo bien abierto, and a shot going into the empty net le pega ahí by accident. El árbitro marca handball. ¿De qué color es la tarjeta?
answer: Red. Denying a goal or an obvious goal-scoring opportunity with a non-deliberate handball offence outside the player's own penalty area is a sending-off offence.
note: L12.4.8 lists the non-deliberate handball outside the own penalty area that denies a goal as a sending-off; L12.4.9 only covers the deliberate case and the non-deliberate case with a penalty.

en: During the first half the fourth official asks a head coach to step back into his technical area. The coach ignores the request but says nothing, and it is the first time it has happened. What action should the referee normally take?
es: En el primer tiempo el cuarto árbitro le pide a un director técnico que regrese a su área técnica. El técnico no le hace caso, pero no dice nada y es la primera vez que pasa. ¿Qué medida debería tomar normalmente el árbitro?
cs: En el primer tiempo the fourth official le pide al coach que se regrese a su technical area. El coach lo ignora, but he doesn't say anything y es la primera vez. ¿Qué hace normalmente el árbitro, a warning or a card?
answer: Normally a warning. Failing to cooperate with a match official, such as ignoring a request from the fourth official, is a warning offence for a team official, with a caution or sending-off kept for repeated or blatant cases.
note: L12.4.13 is the team-official warning list and names ignoring a fourth official's request, plus occasionally leaving the technical area, as warning offences.

en: The goalkeeper catches a cross and keeps hold of the ball for far too long. How does the referee signal that time is running out, what is the restart if the keeper still does not release it, and from exactly where is it taken?
es: El portero atrapa un centro y se queda con el balón en las manos demasiado tiempo. ¿Cómo le avisa el árbitro que se le acaba el tiempo, con qué se reanuda si no lo suelta, y desde dónde exactamente se cobra?
cs: El portero atrapa un centro and just holds the ball way too long. ¿Cómo le avisa el árbitro that time is running out, cuál es el restart si no la suelta, and from where exactly se cobra?
answer: The referee counts down the last five of the eight seconds with a raised hand; holding on longer gives a corner kick, taken from the corner area nearest to the goalkeeper's position when penalised.
note: L12.3 gives the eight-second limit, the visual countdown and the corner kick; L17.1 gives which corner the ball is placed in; also: L17.0 repeats the award but not the countdown.

en: The referee whistles a defender for playing in a dangerous manner near the edge of his own box, with no contact made. The attacking team's taker shoots the free kick straight into the net without anyone else touching it. Does the goal stand, and if not, how does play restart?
es: El árbitro le marca juego peligroso a un defensa cerca del borde de su área, sin que haya contacto. El cobrador del equipo atacante patea el tiro libre directo a la red sin que nadie más toque el balón. ¿Vale el gol? Y si no, ¿cómo se reanuda el juego?
cs: El árbitro le marca dangerous play a un defensa near the edge of his own box, no contact. El otro equipo shoots the free kick directo a la red and nobody else touches it. ¿Vale el gol? And if not, ¿cómo se reanuda?
answer: No goal. Playing in a dangerous manner is punished with an indirect free kick, and an indirect free kick kicked directly into the opponents' goal results in a goal kick.
note: L12.2.0 makes dangerous play an indirect free kick offence and L13.1.2 says what happens when an indirect free kick goes directly into the opponents' goal; also: L12.2.1 defines dangerous play.

en: With the ball in play, an angry assistant coach deliberately throws a water bottle onto the field and it hits the ball in midfield. What happens to the coach, and how does play restart?
es: Con el balón en juego, un auxiliar técnico enojado avienta a propósito una botella de agua a la cancha y le pega al balón en el medio campo. ¿Qué le pasa al auxiliar y cómo se reanuda el juego?
cs: Con el balón en juego, an angry assistant coach avienta una botella de agua onto the field a propósito and it hits the ball en el medio campo. ¿Qué le pasa al coach, and how does play restart?
answer: The coach is sent off, because deliberately throwing an object onto the field of play is a sending-off offence for a team official, and play restarts with a direct free kick from where the bottle struck the ball.
note: L12.4.15 gives the team-official sending-off for deliberately throwing an object onto the field and L12.5 (last paragraph) gives the direct free kick where the object interfered with play.

en: A defender mistimes a tackle and carelessly trips an attacker inside the defender's own penalty area, out wide with no promising attack on. What is the restart, and does the defender need a card?
es: Un defensa llega tarde y por imprudencia le mete una zancadilla a un atacante dentro de su propia área, pegado a la banda y sin ninguna jugada de peligro. ¿Con qué se reanuda el juego y hace falta sacarle tarjeta al defensa?
cs: Un defensa llega tarde and carelessly trips an attacker dentro de su propia área, out wide with nothing really on. ¿Cuál es el restart, y necesita tarjeta or not?
answer: A penalty kick and no card: a careless trip is a direct free kick offence that needs no disciplinary sanction, and a direct free kick offence inside the offender's own penalty area is punished with a penalty kick.
note: L12.1.0 makes a careless trip a direct free kick offence with no sanction and L14.0 turns a direct free kick offence inside the own penalty area into a penalty kick.

en: What's the minimum number of players a team needs for a match to start or keep going?
es: ¿Con cuántos jugadores como mínimo puede un equipo empezar o seguir un partido?
cs: ¿Cuál es el mínimo de players que necesita un equipo para que el partido can start or keep going?
answer: Seven. A match may not start or continue if either team has fewer than seven players.
note: L3.1 sets the eleven-player maximum and the seven-player minimum for starting or continuing a match.

en: Are referees allowed to wear body cameras during a match?
es: ¿Los árbitros pueden llevar cámaras corporales durante el partido?
cs: ¿Los refs pueden usar body cams durante el partido, or is that not allowed?
answer: Yes, if the competition organiser supplies the cameras, controls the footage and follows the relevant guidelines. The cameras may have microphones, but those cannot be used to broadcast communication with the VAR.
note: L5.5.2 lists body cameras among the optional referee equipment and gives the conditions for using them.

en: Where does a goal kick have to be taken from, and when is the ball in play?
es: ¿Desde dónde se tiene que cobrar el saque de meta y en qué momento ya está en juego el balón?
cs: ¿Desde dónde se cobra el goal kick, and when is the ball officially en juego?
answer: From any point inside the goal area, with the ball stationary, by a player of the defending team. The ball is in play as soon as it is kicked and clearly moves.
note: L16.1 is the goal kick procedure: where the kick is taken, when the ball is in play and where opponents must be.

en: Does the team captain have any special rights with the referee?
es: ¿El capitán del equipo tiene algún derecho especial ante el árbitro?
cs: ¿El capitán tiene some kind of special rights con el árbitro, or is he just another player?
answer: No. Each team must have a captain on the field wearing an armband, but the captain has no special status or privileges, only a degree of responsibility for the team's behaviour.
note: L3.10 defines the captain's role and says the captain has no special status; it also mentions the optional 'Only the captain' guidelines.

en: What kinds of decisions can the VAR step in on?
es: ¿En qué tipo de jugadas puede intervenir el VAR?
cs: ¿En qué tipo de jugadas can the VAR actually step in?
answer: Only clear and obvious errors or serious missed incidents about goal or no goal, penalty or no penalty, red cards (including a clearly wrong second caution) and mistaken identity. As a competition option it also covers a clearly wrong corner kick award that can be corrected immediately without delaying the restart.
note: L5.4.0 lists the categories of decision in which the VAR may assist the referee.

en: Why does the ref sometimes hold the whistle after a foul when stopping things would only hurt the side that got fouled, and can he still call it a moment later if nothing comes of it?
es: ¿Por qué a veces el silbante se guarda el pitazo después de una falta cuando marcarla perjudicaría al que la recibió, y todavía la marca un momento después si no salió nada?
cs: ¿Por qué a veces the ref se guarda el pitazo after a foul, cuando marcarla would only hurt al que la recibió? And can he still call it un momento después si no salió nada?
answer: The referee lets the game go on when the fouled team would be better off that way. If the expected benefit does not materialise right then or within a few seconds, the referee goes back and penalises the original offence.
note: L5.3.1 is the advantage clause. Avoided EN: advantage, play, continue, offence, benefit, penalise, opposing, team, seconds, restart, ball. Avoided ES: ventaja, juego, prosiga, infracción, equipo, adversario, beneficiar, sancionar, segundos, reanudación, balón. Also: G.football-terms.advantage (definition only).

en: Can a defender swap jobs with the teammate who guards the net in the middle of a match, and what has to happen for that to be allowed?
es: ¿Se vale que un defensa se ponga los guantes y se pase al arco en lugar del portero a medio partido? ¿Qué hace falta para que sea legal?
cs: ¿Se vale que un defensa swap jobs con el portero in the middle of a match? What has to happen para que sea legal?
answer: Yes. Any player may trade positions with the goalkeeper as long as the referee is told beforehand and the switch happens while play is stopped.
note: L3.4 gives the two conditions for a player changing places with the goalkeeper. Avoided EN: goalkeeper, keeper, change, places, player, referee, informed, stoppage, play. Avoided ES: guardameta, intercambiar, cambio, puesto, jugador, árbitro, informar, juego, detenido. Also: L3.5 (covers only the sanction when it is done without permission).

en: How does the match get going again when a forward's shot misses and leaves the pitch at the end, beside the net, with no defender getting a piece of it?
es: ¿Cómo se reinicia el partido cuando un delantero tira desviado y la pelota sale por el fondo, a un lado del arco, sin que ningún defensa la roce?
cs: ¿Cómo se reinicia el partido when a forward's shot misses y la pelota sale por el fondo, a un lado del arco, with no defender getting a piece of it?
answer: With a goal kick for the defending team, because the whole ball crossed the goal line last touched by an attacker and no goal was scored.
note: L16.0 states when a goal kick is awarded. Avoided EN: goal, kick, awarded, ball, line, touched, player, attacking, team, scored, corner, opponents. Avoided ES: saque, meta, balón, línea, tocar, jugador, equipo, atacante, gol, portería, adversario, esquina.

en: If whoever has the whistle calls the whole thing off because of a storm and somebody ends up hurt or out of pocket, can they sue him over it?
es: Si el silbante cancela todo por una tormenta y alguien sale lastimado o le cuesta dinero, ¿hay manera de demandarlo?
cs: Si el silbante calls the whole thing off por una tormenta and somebody ends up lastimado o le cuesta dinero, can they sue him?
answer: No. Under the Laws a referee or other match official is not held liable for injury, property damage or any other loss that results from a decision made under the Laws, and abandoning a match or judging the weather are named examples.
note: L5.7 is the liability clause for match officials. Avoided EN: referee, match, official, liable, injury, damage, property, loss, decision, weather, conditions, abandon, player, spectator, club. Avoided ES: árbitro, equipo arbitral, responsable, lesión, daño, propiedad, pérdida, decisión, partido, condiciones meteorológicas, suspender, jugador, espectador, club.

en: If someone in the starting eleven is shown a red card during warm-ups, does his side begin a man short or can somebody from the bench step in?
es: Si a un titular le sacan la roja en el calentamiento, ¿su cuadro arranca con diez o entra alguien de la banca en su lugar?
cs: Si a un titular le sacan la roja during warm-ups, ¿su cuadro arranca con diez or can somebody from the bench step in?
answer: A player sent off after the team list is in but before kick-off may be replaced by a named substitute, which means the team can still start with eleven. That substitute's spot on the bench cannot be refilled, and the team's number of substitutions is not reduced.
note: L3.6 covers players sent off before the team list, between the list and kick-off, and after kick-off. Avoided EN: player, sent off, team list, named, kick-off, replaced, substitute, substitutions, number, reduced. Avoided ES: jugador, expulsado, lista, equipo, inscrito, saque inicial, sustituido, suplente, sustituciones, número, reducir. Also: L5.3.2 (gives the referee's authority before kick-off but not the replacement rule).

en: A substitute warming up along the touchline steps onto the field near midfield and kicks away a pass meant for an opposing winger. The referee stops play. What is the restart, and what happens to the substitute?
es: Un suplente que está calentando junto a la banda se mete a la cancha cerca del medio campo y desvía un pase que iba para un extremo rival. El árbitro detiene el juego. ¿Cómo se reanuda y qué pasa con el suplente?
cs: Un suplente que estaba warming up junto a la banda se mete a la cancha near midfield y desvía un pase que iba para un winger del otro equipo. El árbitro para el juego. What's the restart, y qué le pasa al sub?
answer: Play restarts with a direct free kick for the opponents (it would be a penalty kick where that applies). The substitute is removed from the field and the referee takes appropriate disciplinary action.
note: L3.7 says interference by a substitute who enters the field is restarted with a direct free kick or penalty kick, with removal and disciplinary action.

en: With his team up 1-0 late in the match, a goalkeeper keeps stalling over a goal kick. The referee blows the whistle and counts down five seconds with a raised hand, and the kick still has not been taken. What is the ruling?
es: Su equipo va ganando 1-0 al final del partido y el portero se tarda a propósito en cobrar un saque de meta. El árbitro pita y hace la cuenta regresiva de cinco segundos con la mano levantada, y el portero sigue sin sacar. ¿Qué se marca?
cs: Su equipo va ganando 1-0 late in the game y el portero keeps stalling en un saque de meta. The ref pita y hace el five-second countdown con la mano arriba, and he still doesn't take it. ¿Qué se marca?
answer: A corner kick is awarded to the opposing team. The goalkeeper is cautioned only if he goes on to excessively delay the restart after the corner kick has been given.
note: L16.2 describes the five-second countdown for a delayed goal kick and the corner kick that follows. Also: L17.0 (lists the delay as a reason for a corner kick but not the countdown or the caution condition).

en: A midfielder is hurt by a reckless tackle and the opponent is shown a yellow card for it. The physio comes on to check him. Does he have to leave the field and wait before coming back?
es: A un mediocampista lo lastiman con una entrada temeraria y al rival le sacan la amarilla por eso. Entra el médico a revisarlo. ¿Tiene que salir de la cancha y esperar para volver a entrar?
cs: A un mediocampista lo lastiman con una entrada temeraria and the other guy gets a yellow for it. Entra el médico to check on him. Does he have to salir de la cancha y esperar before coming back in?
answer: No. A player whose injury stops play normally has to leave and may return only one minute after play restarts, but one of the listed exceptions is an injury caused by a physical offence for which the opponent is cautioned or sent off.
note: L5.3.3 holds the leave-the-field requirement for injured players and its list of exceptions, including the cautioned-opponent case.

en: A team scores, and before the kick-off the referee realises that a player of that team who had already been substituted was still on the field and helped set up the goal. What should the referee do?
es: Un equipo mete gol y, antes de que se saque del centro, el árbitro se da cuenta de que un jugador de ese equipo que ya había sido cambiado seguía dentro de la cancha y participó en la jugada del gol. ¿Qué debe hacer el árbitro?
cs: Un equipo mete gol and before the kick-off el árbitro se da cuenta de que un jugador de ese equipo who had already been subbed off seguía en la cancha y participó en la jugada. What should the ref do?
answer: Disallow the goal, have the substituted player removed, and restart with a direct free kick from the position where that extra person was. The incident is also reported to the authorities.
note: L3.9 covers a goal scored with an extra person on the field who interfered, when it is noticed before play restarts, including the case where that person belongs to the scoring team.

en: The substitution board goes up, but the player coming off walks slowly and is still on the field after ten seconds, with no injury or safety issue. What happens with the substitution?
es: Muestran el tablero del cambio, pero el jugador que sale se va caminando despacio y a los diez segundos sigue dentro de la cancha, sin estar lesionado ni haber un problema de seguridad. ¿Qué pasa con el cambio?
cs: Sacan el tablero del cambio, but the guy coming off se va caminando bien lento and after ten seconds sigue dentro de la cancha, no injury ni nada. ¿Qué pasa con el cambio?
answer: The player must still leave, but the substitute may not come on yet and play restarts without him. The substitution cannot be cancelled or switched to another substitute, and the substitute may enter with the referee's permission at the first stoppage after one minute has passed since the restart; the departing player is cautioned only for excessive delay beyond the ten seconds.
note: L3.5 lists the consequences when the player being substituted does not leave within the required ten seconds. Also: L3.3 (sets the ten-second requirement but not the consequences).

en: Play has already restarted when the referee finds out that a player punched an opponent off the ball. Can the referee still send that player off, and in what situations?
es: El juego ya se reanudó cuando el árbitro se entera de que un jugador le dio un puñetazo a un rival lejos del balón. ¿Todavía lo puede expulsar, y en qué casos?
cs: El juego ya se reanudó when the ref finds out que un jugador le soltó un puñetazo a un rival off the ball. Can he still expulsarlo, y en qué casos?
answer: Yes, in limited cases. A sanction after the restart is possible if another match official had spotted the offence and tried to communicate it before play restarted, and where VAR is in use a review after a restart is still allowed for a potential sending-off for violent conduct. The restart tied to the offence is not applied.
note: L5.2 gives the general limit on sanctions after a restart and the other-match-official exception; L5.4.1 gives the VAR exception for violent conduct after play has restarted.

en: A goal kick is caught by a strong wind and blows straight back into the kicker's own goal without anyone touching it. What is the restart, and if the other team then puts that restart straight into the net, does it count?
es: Un saque de meta agarra un ventarrón y el balón se regresa directo a la portería del mismo equipo que sacó, sin que nadie lo toque. ¿Cómo se reanuda el juego? Y si el rival mete ese cobro directo a la red, ¿cuenta el gol?
cs: Un saque de meta agarra un ventarrón and the ball goes straight back a la portería del mismo equipo, sin que nadie lo toque. What's the restart? Y si el otro equipo lo mete directo, does the goal count?
answer: There is no own goal; the opponents are awarded a corner kick. A goal may be scored directly from a corner kick against the opposing team, and that goal counts.
note: L16.0 says a goal kick that goes directly into the kicker's own goal gives a corner kick to the opponents; L17.0 says a goal can be scored directly from a corner kick against the opposing team.

en: A fan blows a whistle and a midfielder stops with the ball at his feet near the centre circle, and the referee stops play. How does play restart, who gets the ball, and how far away must everyone else be?
es: Alguien en la tribuna suena un silbato y un mediocampista se frena con el balón en los pies cerca del círculo central, y el árbitro detiene el juego. ¿Cómo se reanuda, a quién le toca el balón y a qué distancia deben estar los demás?
cs: Alguien en la tribuna blows a whistle y un mediocampista se frena con el balón en los pies near the center circle, and the ref para el juego. ¿Cómo se reanuda, who gets the ball, y a qué distancia tienen que estar los demás?
answer: With a dropped ball. Because the ball was outside the penalty area, it is dropped where it was for one player of the team that would have kept possession, and all other players must stay at least 4 m (4.5 yds) away until it is in play.
note: L5.3.4 says a spectator's whistle that interferes with play leads to a dropped ball; L8.2.1 says who receives the dropped ball, where it is dropped and the 4 m distance.

en: A defender is sent to the sideline because of a bleeding cut. Without waiting for the referee's signal he runs back on and intercepts a pass. What does the referee do, and how does play restart?
es: A un defensa lo mandan fuera de la cancha porque trae una cortada que le sangra. Sin esperar la señal del árbitro se vuelve a meter y corta un pase. ¿Qué hace el árbitro y cómo se reanuda el juego?
cs: A un defensa lo sacan de la cancha because he's bleeding de una cortada. Sin esperar la señal del ref he runs back on y corta un pase. What does the ref do, y cómo se reanuda el juego?
answer: A bleeding player may only come back on the referee's signal. Since he re-entered without permission and interfered with play, the referee stops play, cautions him, and restarts with a direct free kick from the position of the interference.
note: L5.3.3 says a bleeding player needs the referee's signal to re-enter; L3.8 gives the caution and the direct free kick for a player who re-enters without permission and interferes.

en: How many timeouts does each coach get to call per half?
es: ¿Cuántos tiempos fuera puede pedir cada entrenador en cada tiempo?
cs: ¿Cuántos timeouts puede pedir cada coach per half?
answer: The Laws give coaches no timeouts at all. Play only stops for the reasons the referee decides, and the only breaks mentioned are half-time and drinks or cooling breaks set by competition rules.
note: False premise is coach-called timeouts borrowed from basketball and American football; searched 'timeout' and 'time-out' with no hits, and the drinks and cooling breaks in L7.2 and L7.3 are not timeouts a coach can call, which is why gold is empty.

en: How many fouls can a player commit before he is automatically out of the game?
es: ¿Cuántas faltas puede cometer un jugador antes de quedar expulsado automáticamente del partido?
cs: ¿Cuántas faltas puede hacer un jugador before he automatically fouls out del partido?
answer: There is no foul count that removes a player. Repeated fouling can earn a caution for persistent offences, and the Laws say no specific number of offences defines persistent.
note: False premise is fouling out after a fixed number of fouls as in basketball; L12.4.4 lists persistent offences as a caution and states that no specific number or pattern applies.

en: From how far out does a shot have to be taken for the goal to count double?
es: ¿Desde qué distancia tiene que ser el disparo para que el gol valga doble?
cs: ¿Desde qué distancia tiene que ser el shot para que el gol count double?
answer: No goal is worth more than one, however far out the shot is taken. The Laws have no rule that ties the value of a goal to distance.
note: False premise is a long-range goal counting double like a three-pointer; searched 'double' and 'distance' and the only hit for double is the away goals glossary entry, which is about venue and not shot distance, which is why gold is empty.

en: How many seconds does a team have to take a shot before the shot clock runs out and the ball goes to the other team?
es: ¿Cuántos segundos tiene un equipo para tirar a gol antes de que se acabe el reloj de posesión y el balón pase al rival?
cs: ¿Cuántos segundos tiene un equipo para tirar antes de que se acabe el shot clock and the ball goes to the other team?
answer: There is no shot clock. The Laws put no time limit on how long a team can keep the ball before shooting.
note: False premise is a possession shot clock from basketball; searched 'clock' with no hits, and the only countdowns in the corpus are for a goalkeeper holding the ball and for delayed restarts, which is why gold is empty.

en: What is the most passes in a row a team can make before it has to shoot?
es: ¿Cuántos pases seguidos puede dar un equipo como máximo antes de estar obligado a tirar a gol?
cs: What's the max de pases seguidos que puede dar un equipo before they have to shoot?
answer: There is no limit. The Laws never restrict how many passes a team can string together.
note: False premise is a cap on consecutive passes; searched 'consecutive', 'passes' and 'passing' and no passage limits passing, which is why gold is empty.

en: Why is it always a straight red card when the last defender commits a foul, even if he was going for the ball inside his own box?
es: ¿Por qué siempre es roja directa cuando el último defensa comete una falta, aunque haya ido al balón dentro de su propia área?
cs: ¿Por qué siempre es roja directa when the last man commits a foul, aunque haya ido al balón inside his own box?
answer: It is not automatic and the Laws have no last-man rule. What matters is whether an obvious goal-scoring opportunity was denied, and when a penalty is given for a genuine attempt to play the ball the defender is only cautioned.
note: False premise is the 'last man is always sent off' myth; L12.4.9 gives the caution for an attempt to play the ball when a penalty is awarded and lists the factors for judging an obvious goal-scoring opportunity, none of which is being the last defender.

en: My teammate threw the ball in to me while I was standing behind the whole defense. Where does the other team take the free kick for my offside?
es: Mi compañero me dio el balón con un saque de banda cuando yo estaba detrás de toda la defensa. ¿Desde dónde cobra el otro equipo el tiro libre por mi fuera de lugar?
cs: Mi compañero me la dio de un throw-in cuando yo estaba behind the whole defense. ¿Dónde cobra el otro equipo el free kick por mi offside?
answer: There is no free kick, because a player cannot be penalised for offside when receiving the ball directly from a throw-in.
note: False premise is that offside applies on a throw-in; L11.3 lists the throw-in among the restarts from which there is no offside offence.

en: When a player scores by throwing the ball straight into the net from a throw-in, does the game restart with a kick-off like after any other goal?
es: Cuando un jugador mete gol directo de un saque de banda, ¿el partido se reanuda con un saque de centro como en cualquier otro gol?
cs: Cuando un jugador mete gol directo de un throw-in, does the game restart con saque de centro like any other goal?
answer: That is not a goal. A goal cannot be scored directly from a throw-in, and if the ball goes straight into the opponents' goal the restart is a goal kick.
note: False premise is that a throw-in thrown straight into the net counts as a goal; L15.0 says it cannot and names the restart for each goal.

en: The keeper held the ball in his hands for more than six seconds. Where does the other team take the indirect free kick?
es: El portero se quedó con el balón en las manos más de seis segundos. ¿Desde dónde cobra el otro equipo el tiro libre indirecto?
cs: El portero held the ball más de seis segundos en las manos. Where does the other team take el tiro libre indirecto?
answer: The limit is eight seconds, not six, and the punishment is not an indirect free kick. The other team gets a corner kick.
note: False premise is the old six-second rule punished with an indirect free kick; L12.3 sets eight seconds and awards a corner kick.

en: Who is in charge of stopping the clock every time the ball goes out of play?
es: ¿Quién se encarga de parar el reloj cada vez que el balón sale del campo?
cs: ¿Quién se encarga de parar el reloj every time the ball goes out of play?
answer: Nobody, because the clock is not stopped when the ball goes out. The referee instead adds time at the end of each half for playing time lost to things like substitutions, injuries and time-wasting.
note: False premise is a stop-clock as in basketball or American football; L7.3 shows that lost time is made up by an allowance the referee adds in each half.

en: How many minutes does each of the four quarters last in an adult match?
es: ¿Cuántos minutos dura cada uno de los cuatro cuartos en un partido de adultos?
cs: ¿Cuántos minutos dura each of the four quarters en un partido de adultos?
answer: A match is not played in quarters. It has two equal halves of 45 minutes.
note: False premise is four quarters as in basketball or American football; L7.1 states the two 45-minute halves.

en: A player on my team got called for trying a bicycle kick with nobody near him. Is the restart for that illegal kick a direct or an indirect free kick?
es: A un jugador de mi equipo le marcaron falta por intentar una chilena sin nadie cerca. ¿La reanudación por esa jugada prohibida es tiro libre directo o indirecto?
cs: A un jugador de mi equipo le marcaron falta for trying a bicycle kick sin nadie cerca. ¿Por esa jugada prohibida es direct free kick o indirecto?
answer: A bicycle kick is not illegal in itself. It is allowed as long as it is not dangerous to an opponent, and with nobody near there is no offence to restart from.
note: False premise is that bicycle or overhead kicks are banned outright; L12.2.1 says a scissors or bicycle kick is permissible provided it is not dangerous to an opponent.

en: How many points does a team get in the league table for a win and for a draw?
es: ¿Cuántos puntos le dan a un equipo en la tabla por ganar y por empatar?
cs: ¿Cuántos puntos te dan en la tabla for a win y por un empate?
answer: Not covered by the Laws of the Game.
note: Searched 'points', 'league', 'table' and 'standings' in laws and glossary; the only related passage, L10.2, says who wins a match and nothing about league points.

es: Si dos equipos terminan la temporada con los mismos puntos, ¿el desempate es por diferencia de goles o por los resultados entre ellos?
cs: Si dos equipos terminan la temporada con los mismos puntos, is the tiebreaker goal difference o los resultados entre ellos?
answer: Not covered by the Laws of the Game.
note: Searched 'goal difference', 'head-to-head', 'points', 'season' and 'league' with no hits; L10.2 and the away goals glossary entry only cover deciding a single match or a home-and-away tie, not a league table.

es: ¿Cuándo cierra el mercado de fichajes de verano para que los clubes contraten jugadores?

answer: Not covered by the Laws of the Game.

cs: ¿Cuántas amarillas tiene que juntar un jugador over the season before he has to sit out el siguiente partido?
answer: Not covered by the Laws of the Game.

es: ¿Cuántos jugadores extranjeros puede registrar un club en su plantel?
cs: ¿Cuántos extranjeros puede registrar un club on its squad?
answer: Not covered by the Laws of the Game.
